clue.text: Sweets possess a male application

parts.note: afters is British slang for the dessert course, the sweets that follow a meal
to possess is to have

explanation.surface: Someone's sweets come with a dab of something for men.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is everyday British for pudding or dessert, the 'sweets' course.
explanation.definitionFit: Men splash this lotion on their faces after shaving, so it is a grooming product applied by males.

clue.text: Loud anger and passion

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: A list of strong emotions: noise, rage and ardour.
explanation.walkthrough: F is forte, the musical direction to play loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent feeling is often called fire, as in speaking with great fire.

clue.text: Rarely seen part of the French president's residence

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The French leader's home is a place the public rarely gets to view.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across rarELY SEEn; the definition is the Elysee Palace in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elysee Palace in Paris is the official home of the head of state of France.

clue.text: Advertising jingles transcribed on glass

indicators.note: transcribed suggests the letters are written out again in a new form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advertising catchphrases have been painted onto a shop window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transcribed' rearranges the seven letters of ON GLASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchy marketing phrases and jingles are both short memorable lines used to sell products.

clue.text: Wild swan seen in a field of barley

definitions.text: seen in a field of barley

indicators.note: wild means the letters of the word swan run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild bird has turned up among the barley crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges SWAN; the definition is descriptive rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the bristly whiskers on ears of barley, a sight across any field of that grain.

clue.text: Guarantees two points to new users

parts.note: E and N are two points of the compass, east and north

indicators.note: new signals that the word users is made afresh with its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A firm promises a couple of loyalty points to anyone signing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges USERS to SURES, which follows E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee something is to make certain of it.

clue.text: The early morning air?

parts.note: air reads as atmosphere but means a tune: the birdsong heard at first light

explanation.surface: A question about the freshness of the atmosphere at daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds sing together at daybreak, and that song is a tune, which is what an air is.

clue.text: Narrow escape-from Sweeney Todd?

explanation.surface: A lucky escape from the murderous barber of Fleet Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is the fictional demon barber of London, who cut his customers' throats; a shave from him would be close in both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is an idiom for a narrow escape, and a barber's razor gives a very smooth trim.

clue.text: Chain letters?

explanation.surface: A question about letters that pass from person to person in a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour of linked metal rings is chain armour, and the post brings letters.

clue.text: We may bet on them to give us hydrogen

indicators.note: give in the sense of yielding or bending out of shape signals that the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry boast about what something will yield for us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give' rearranges US plus HYDROGEN, ten letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing dogs are a staple of betting at the track.

clue.text: Tips union leader to spend freely

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of union
freely suggests the letters of spend move about at will into another order

explanation.surface: A trade union boss advises members to splash out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes U from union; 'freely' rearranges SPEND to PENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip something over is to turn it upside down.

clue.text: Cattle feed in the lake

explanation.surface: Livestock fodder floating in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucerne is the British name for alfalfa, a fodder crop, and also a lake in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfalfa is a fodder plant grown for livestock, and a Swiss lake shares its name.

clue.text: They shelve their responsibilities

parts.note: shelving responsibilities sounds like shirking duty but literally means putting books on shelves

explanation.surface: People who dodge their duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff in a lending institution place books back on racks as their daily work.

clue.text: Bird comes down to earth, target for a marksman

indicators.note: in a down clue the bird word descends to sit below the earth word

parts.note: clay is a kind of earth or soil
a pigeon is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird lands on the ground and becomes a shooter's target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes down to' places PIGEON beneath CLAY in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay discs flung into the air are what trap shooters fire at.

clue.text: Number of men seen on the river

explanation.surface: A count of oarsmen out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing, a crew of oarsmen in one boat is named for its size.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a numeral, and also a rowing boat crewed by that many oarsmen.

clue.text: Every set-back about it is instructive

indicators.note: about says the reversed word wraps around the other piece
back after set says that word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
every means each

explanation.surface: A setback concerning it teaches a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SET into TES, and 'about' puts it round EACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that instructs gives lessons, so it is educational in the same sense.

clue.text: It's up for approval

parts.note: up for approval suggests awaiting a vote but means the digit raised to show consent

explanation.surface: Something waiting to be voted through.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising this digit is a gesture of consent or approval.

clue.text: Sounds of relief of audible dimensions

indicators.note: audible says the word is heard rather than read, so its sound counts

parts.note: dimensions give the size of something

explanation.surface: Relieved exhalations loud enough to measure.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGHS is said the same way as SIZE, signalled by 'audible'.
explanation.definitionFit: Long breaths let out when tension eases are relieved exhalations.

clue.text: Bill may be a magistrate

explanation.surface: An invoice could turn out to be a justice of the peace.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAK is old British slang for a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's bill is its beak, and British slang uses the same word for a judge in a lower court.

clue.text: It could be for a Malayan vessel

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: Something might suit a boat from Malaysia.
explanation.walkthrough: A proa is a fast sailing boat of the Malay region.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fast outrigger sailing craft from the Malay archipelago.

clue.text: Much changed party-leader isa fool

indicators.note: changed signals that the letters of much are rearranged
the leader of party is its first letter

explanation.surface: A political leader much altered is now an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges MUCH to CHUM; 'leader' adds P from party. The page prints 'isa' for 'is a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chump is an informal word for a silly person or idiot.

clue.text: A number beaten in the final

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
beaten means losing

explanation.surface: A team is beaten in the cup final.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the Roman numeral 100, a 'number'.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing means coming last, as in the closing scene of a play.

clue.text: Continue with the ironing

explanation.surface: Carry on with pressing the clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to keep going, and smoothing clothes with an iron is pressing them.

clue.text: Pitch of the roof?

parts.note: pitch reads as the slope of a roof but means the tarry black substance used for roofing

explanation.surface: A builder asks about the slope of a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitumen or tar, the black sticky substance, is spread on flat roofs and roads.

clue.text: Money that is shortly required for the club

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Some cash is needed to join the club.
explanation.walkthrough: BRASS is northern British slang for cash; a brassie is an old name for a wooden golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassie is an old wooden golf club, roughly a two-wood, with a brass sole plate.

clue.text: Grievance in this way starts a right squabble

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: starts takes the first letter of right

parts.note: a row is a squabble

explanation.surface: Doing it like this sets off a proper argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' gives R, the first letter of 'right'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow is distress or grief, a cause of complaint here in an older sense of grievance.

clue.text: Mint bars?

parts.note: mint bars suggests chocolate confections but means metal blocks from a place where coins are made

explanation.surface: A question about peppermint chocolate bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast blocks of gold or silver are produced by a mint or bullion refiner.

clue.text: Albert shortly gets to be a singer

parts.note: Al is a short form of the name Albert
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bert in brief makes it as a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: AL is the shortened name of Albert.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a voice part, the lowest female or highest adult male range, so a vocalist.

clue.text: Leading performer you can't see any day

explanation.surface: A headline act whom you cannot catch on any day.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars are invisible in daylight, giving the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The headline actor is a celebrity; heavenly lights are hidden by sunlight in daytime.

clue.text: Show it's all true, strangely enough

indicators.note: strangely enough says the letters of the words fall into an odd new order

parts.note: the letters of it's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Proving that the whole story is factual, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely enough' rearranges ITS ALL TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to demonstrate it with examples.

clue.text: High time for a Western

parts.note: high time suggests urgency, but points to the hour in the title of a classic cowboy film

explanation.surface: It's about time someone made a cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: High Noon (1952) is a famous Western film.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is high noon, the hour of the showdown in that classic cowboy film.

clue.text: Preparation requiring land and labour

parts.note: ground means land
work means labour

explanation.surface: Getting ready takes both soil and toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic preliminary effort laying a base for later is preparation.
